page: Microsoft Azure E16-8as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing the AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system pairs these compute resources with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, 32 MB of L3 cache, standard x86_64 instruction extensions such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, and a bundled 275 GB local SSD. It includes no discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier execution across typical enterprise workloads, recording a Geekbench 6 single-core score of 1604.0, a multi-core score of 6375.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 11895.86. The architecture delivers 8.29 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and achieves 10.12 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Compute-intensive vectorization and uncached memory throughput are less competitive; uncached read and write bandwidths measure 39.27 GB/sec and 22.62 GB/sec respectively, alongside a multi-core stress-ng rating in the lower quartile.

The constrained vCPU configuration offers high cost efficiency for software environments licensed per core, such as relational databases, by maintaining 128 GB of memory alongside only 8 active vCPUs. Tradeoffs involve reduced raw multi-core throughput and limited inference performance on medium language models. The machine is best suited for memory-bound relational databases, in-memory caching platforms, and data processing tasks requiring substantial RAM per core without massive parallel thread counts.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-8as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. Configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 128.0 GB of memory, the instance delivers a high 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio, complemented by 275 GB of local SSD temporary storage and no discrete GPU. In benchmark assessments, it achieves 8.29 million Redis SET operations per second and steady general-purpose performance, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 6375.0 and PassMark database score of 3658.57. Because it pairs high memory density with a reduced vCPU count, the instance is cost-efficient for core-licensed database software, enterprise caching, and memory-heavy analytics pipelines where memory capacity takes precedence over aggregate multi-core compute throughput.
